target_customer: Marketing and growth teams at companies that keep customer data in a cloud warehouse such as BigQuery or Snowflake
problem: Customer engagement tools like Braze copy and store customer data, which costs money and creates silos. Castled runs on the warehouse instead.
business_model: B2B SaaS, warehouse-native customer engagement platform with an alternative pricing model

founders.background_notes: Source: YC page. Not named in the YC launch post.

founders.background_notes: Built and scaled enterprise storage systems per YC page. Called Frank in the launch post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Segmentation and multichannel messaging directly on warehouses means building connectors to several warehouses and delivery channels, with some hard performance work, but all established engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Established CEP vendors and reverse ETL tools such as Hightouch and Census could add warehouse-native segmentation. Integrations create some switching costs once campaigns run.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in the sources read. Castled's own blog compared itself with Hightouch and Census, showing reverse ETL rivals in the same wedge.

market_need_then: Marketers wanted to use warehouse data directly; the founders said in their launch post they spoke to hundreds of marketers and claimed 75 percent lower cost than a traditional marketing tool (a company claim).

branding.domain_note: Uses castled.io rather than an exact .com

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and cost-focused founder blog posts on Medium

branding.community_and_virality: Open source reverse ETL repo and Medium blog posts; a Show HN repost dated June 2023 exists. No evidence of fan or meme activity.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. The name is easy to confuse with the unrelated Castle.io and castlabs.

pivots.from: Open source reverse ETL tool (cloud launch about October 2021)
pivots.why: A June 2023 Show HN repost says the team changed course to build a warehouse-first engagement product; date is approximate and the repost site is not authoritative

outcome_analysis: Castled started in 2021 with open source reverse ETL, then moved to warehouse-native customer engagement against Braze and similar vendors while Hightouch and Census occupied the adjacent wedge. YC lists the company as inactive, and no shutdown post, acquisition or layoffs report was found, so the cause of inactivity is not public.
notes: Website castled.io returned HTTP 503 on fetch. The US$2.1M seed rests on one aggregator (Employbl, data from Diffbot) with no date and no cross-check found. Exit is unknown because the YC status is Inactive but no source states what happened. Launch post exact date not shown (about four years ago). Competitors are named on the YC page and launch post, with no dated traction found. Founder education not found.
